title: The Goodness of God
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The goodness of God means that God is good in Himself and does good toward His creation and people. His goodness is generous, wise, holy, faithful, and worthy of trust.
summary: The goodness of God means that God is good in Himself and does good toward His creation and people. His goodness is generous, wise, holy, faithful, and worthy of trust.
christFocus: Jesus Christ reveals the goodness of God by bringing mercy, truth, healing, forgiveness, and salvation to sinners. In Christ, believers taste and see that the Lord is good.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God is good by nature. His goodness is not occasional or accidental. It belongs to who He is. All that is truly good comes from Him and reflects His generous character.

God’s goodness is seen in creation, provision, patience, mercy, correction, and salvation. Every good and perfect gift comes from above, from the Father who does not shift like shadows.

The goodness of God is not shallow comfort. God’s goodness is holy and wise. He may show goodness through blessing, but also through correction, patience, and kindness that leads people to repentance.

Moses asked to see God’s glory, and God made His goodness pass before him. God’s goodness is tied to His glory, mercy, compassion, and sovereign freedom. In Christ, that goodness is displayed in saving grace.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Suffering can make people question whether God is good. This doctrine does not deny pain or pretend evil is good. It anchors believers in the character of God when circumstances are confusing.

God’s goodness also confronts suspicion. The serpent’s first lie questioned whether God was truly good. Faith learns to trust God’s goodness as revealed in His Word and especially in Christ.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Taste and see that the Lord is good. Give thanks for His gifts, trust Him when His ways are hard, and let His kindness lead you to repentance. Do not measure God’s goodness only by comfort; measure it by His character and the cross of Christ.
